## Goal

Make `implement.py finish` **fail closed** when a worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist` — an actionable error naming the stale path and remediation, so a green gate never silently passes on the wrong code. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

## Problem (parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO)

`phase_finish` runs build → test gate → commit from the worktree. If resolution is stale (worktree's `@worklog/shared` → main checkout's `packages/shared/dist`), the gate either false-reds on correct new code (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) or false-greens on broken code. The gate currently cannot distinguish "shared code changed in this worktree" from "shared code unchanged" and exposes no resolution diagnostic.

## Desired change (producer-decided: hard-fail)

1. Extract the resolution check from the F2 link-farm feature into a shared helper (`@worklog/shared` resolved package root == `<worktree>/packages/shared`), reused by the `start` JSON report and `finish`.
2. In `phase_finish`, before the test gate (after the build step), compute whether the worktree diff touches `packages/shared/src/**` and whether the resolution check fails; when both hold, hard-fail with a message naming the stale `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation (re-run `implement.py start` / the documented refresh command from the main checkout, then rebuild).
3. End-to-end probe verification (AC1): in a fresh worktree, a probe change under `packages/shared/src/**` is observed by the sanctioned gate (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`), and an unmodified main checkout would not observe it.
4. Detection no-ops for repos without a workspace shared package (degradation path).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `finish` hard-fails (non-zero, no commit, item released to `open` with the failure comment) with an actionable message naming the stale `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation when the worktree diff touches `packages/shared/src/**` AND the resolution check fails — covered by the F1 negative-path test.
2. The gate passes normally when the resolution check succeeds (worktree-local link farm present), including when shared source is unchanged.
3. The e2e probe proves the worktree's `packages/shared/src/**` change is observed by the gate (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`) from inside a fresh worktree, and that an unmodified main checkout does not observe it.
4. The resolution helper is shared between `start` and `finish` (single source of truth), and its detection logic is covered by the F1 unit tests.
5. No change to main-checkout build/test behaviour (byte-for-byte unchanged outside worktree setups); the main checkout stays git-clean of non-gitignored artefacts after start → build → gate → finish.

- **Traceability (parent AC4):** **Hard-fail on stale resolution.** `implement.py finish` (build → test gate)
## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_stale_shared_resolution.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_node_modules_link_farm.py`

## Related

- Parent SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO; F2 link-farm dependency; false-red case WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO (ContextHub); predecessor verification WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2 / SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B.

- **Traceability (parent AC4):** **Hard-fail on stale resolution.** `implement.py finish` (build → test gate)

# Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review

**Headline:** The audit runner must stop re-arming `needsProducerReview` on a
passing re-audit of an item the producer has already reviewed, and must start
setting it on any failing (`Ready to close: No`) top-level audit — so a
producer's review survives a release-time re-audit while genuine failures
always reach the producer queue.

## Problem statement

On 2026-10-27 a `dev`→`main` release of the ContextHub store was blocked
because the audit runner re-flagged 14 top-level `in_review` items for producer
review. The producer had already reviewed and cleared those items; the release's
own re-audits all **passed**, and each pass unconditionally wrote
`--needs-producer-review yes`, silently discarding the producer's review.
Inversely, the failing-verdict path only flags an item when
`merge_gate_blocker` is set, so genuinely failing items never reach the
producer-review queue. The review state is unobservable after the fact because
`needsProducerReview` is a bare boolean and flag-only flips neither bump
`updatedAt` nor leave any record.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — the person who reviews and clears items before
  release. *"As a producer I want a review I have given to stay given until the
  item's content actually changes, so that I am not asked to re-approve the same
  unchanged work every time a release re-audits it."*
- **Producer, failure path** — *"As a producer I want every item whose audit says
  `Ready to close: No` surfaced to me, so that a failing item cannot sit
  silently in the actionable queue."*
- **Release gate (ship skill)** — *"As the release gate I want
  `needsProducerReview` to mean exactly 'this item needs producer attention now',
  so that the gate neither blocks on already-reviewed work nor passes
  unreviewed/unready work."*
- **Audit runner (agent)** — *"As the audit runner I want an unambiguous rule for
  when to set the flag, so that pass/fail lifecycles stay deterministic and
  auditable."*

## Target behaviour

| Verdict | Item | Prior producer review (signal present) | `needsProducerReview` after the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | yes (reviewed, content unchanged since review) | **left `false`** (do not re-flag) |
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | no (never reviewed, or content changed since review) | **`yes`** (current behaviour) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level (independent audit) | either | **`yes`** (generalise the merge-gate branch) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level, cascade-demotion-suppressed (parent-triggered re-audit of an `in_review`/`done` item) | either | **unchanged / never set** (producer decision, Q2 = no) |
| any | child (has parent) | either | **unchanged / never set** (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H) |

> **Cascade rule (producer decision Q2 = no).** A `No` produced by a
> parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item is not
> an independent review: the demotion is suppressed (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) and the
> flag is likewise left untouched. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the
> item to the producer.

Existing lifecycle guarantees are unchanged: pre-audit status/stage restore on
abort and on infrastructure failure, `updatedAt = auditedAt` on audit persist,
assignee clear-on-terminal, and the descendant cascade authorised only by a
verified `Yes`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (reviewed pass is preserved).** A passing verdict (`Ready to close: Yes`)
  on a top-level item whose producer has already reviewed it (and whose content
  is unchanged since that review) does not write
  `--needs-producer-review yes`; the stored `false` is preserved and the item is
  not re-entered into the producer-review queue.
- **AC2 (first pass still enters the queue).** A passing verdict on a top-level
  item that has never been reviewed still sets `needsProducerReview = yes`.
- **AC3 (independent failures always surface).** A failing verdict
  (`Ready to close: No`) from an **independent** audit of a top-level item sets
  `needsProducerReview = yes` regardless of whether `merge_gate_blocker` is set,
  and never clears an existing review. The single exception is the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed branch (Q2 = no): a parent-triggered re-audit of an
  already-`in_review`/`done` item leaves the flag untouched.
- **AC4 (signal is durable, auditable and content-scoped).** The review state used
  by AC1/AC3 distinguishes *"reviewed and cleared"* from *"never flagged"*, is
  recorded somewhere a later run (and a human) can inspect, and is invalidated
  when the item's reviewed content changes — so a materially changed item
  requires a fresh producer review.
- **AC5 (transitions covered by tests in the default suite).** Regression tests
  cover all four transitions — never-reviewed pass → flagged; reviewed pass →
  preserved; fail → flagged (with and without `merge_gate_blocker`); review →
  content change → pass → flagged again — plus the child exemption (AC6), the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed `No` → **unchanged** (Q2), and "`wl audit-show`
  unavailable ⇒ flagged" (fail-safe) — and run in the default suite
  (`skill/audit/tests/`, no marker gating).
- **AC6 (children unchanged).** A passing verdict on a child item never sets
  `needsProducerReview`, and no child-item lifecycle behaviour changes.
- **AC7 (no lifecycle regressions).** The existing guarantees hold: pre-audit
  status/stage restore on abort and infrastructure failure, `updatedAt =
  auditedAt` on audit persist, assignee clear-on-terminal, cascade-demotion
  suppression, and the lifecycle readback verification.
- **AC8 (docs).** The audit skill's reference documentation
  (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` lifecycle section)
  states the pass/fail flag semantics explicitly, including that producer review
  is **content-scoped** and how a cleared flag is distinguished from a
  never-flagged item.
- **AC9 (documentation currency).** All related documentation **in this
  repository** is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and `docs/dev/` entries. ContextHub's `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` is out of
  scope — this item makes no cross-repo change (see *Key Files*).
- **AC10 (suite).** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Review-state signal — DECIDED: Option B+ (producer, 2026-10-28)

`needsProducerReview` alone cannot answer *"was this reviewed?"*. Two candidate
designs were carried into intake; the seed context marked Option A as preferred,
but the repository evidence gathered during intake changed the cost/benefit
picture (see *Existing state*), so the choice was put to the producer
(Appendix Q1). **Producer chose Option B+** — inference with the persisted-report
recap. Option A-lite remains a possible later upgrade but is **not** part of this
item's scope; it does not need to be raised as a dependency.

### Option B+ — infer from existing state, recap in the persisted report (no cross-repo change) — CHOSEN

At audit start, capture the item's pre-audit audit record (`readyToClose` +
`fingerprint`, both already exposed by `wl audit-show --json`) alongside the
existing pre-audit `wl show` capture. Then:

- prior audit `readyToClose == 1` **and** its fingerprint equals the current
  content fingerprint **and** the item's `needsProducerReview == false`
  → the flag can only have been cleared by a producer *after* that passing
  audit of identical content → **preserve `false`**;
- otherwise (no prior audit, prior audit failed, or content changed since the
  passing audit) → **flag `yes`**;
- `needsProducerReview == true` is never cleared by the runner.

Because the audit content fingerprint is already content-scoped (schema-2
sha256 over the item's own `title` + `description`), this option satisfies AC4's
*content-scoped* requirement with no schema change. For auditability, the runner
appends an explicit metadata line to the report it persists anyway
(e.g. `Producer review: preserved (content fingerprint <fp>)` /
`Producer review: required (reason)`), so the decision is recorded in the
durable audit record.

### Option A-lite — durable review marker in the worklog store (cross-repo; NOT chosen)

Add a nullable marker (e.g. `audit_results.producer_reviewed_fingerprint` +
`producer_reviewed_at`, or `work_items.producerReviewedAt`) written whenever
`needsProducerReview` transitions `true → false`. The audit runner then compares
the stored reviewed fingerprint with the current one: equal → preserve `false`;
different/absent → flag `yes`.

This is exact and self-documenting, but it is a ContextHub worklog change:
schema migration + repair-on-open + the marker must be written on **every**
clear path (`wl reviewed <id> false`, `wl update --needs-producer-review false`
used by the ship gate's remediation text, the ship override that clears child
flags, and any future path). It also creates a cross-repo blocking dependency
for this item.

**Cost signal:** Option B+ is a single-repo change (one lifecycle region, one
helper, tests, docs); Option A-lite additionally requires a ContextHub work
item, migration, CLI surface and its own audit. Option B+ can be upgraded to
Option A-lite later without changing this item's acceptance criteria for the
pass/fail rules. **Not chosen by the producer — no ContextHub dependency is
raised by this item.**

## Constraints

- **Do not revert the pass-flag contract.** SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5 and
  SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW established that an automated pass puts a top-level item in
  the producer queue; this item refines *when*, not *whether*.
- **Never clear a review silently.** The runner may preserve `false`; it must not
  write `--needs-producer-review no` on any path.
- **Fail-safe direction.** When the review signal is ambiguous or unavailable
  (e.g. `wl audit-show` fails, legacy fingerprint-less audit), the runner must
  fall back to **flagging** (`yes`) — a spurious review request is a nuisance; a
  silently discarded review gate is a release-safety defect.
- **Bias to fewer `wl` calls.** No new per-item `wl` invocation on the hot path
  where the existing freshness gate already fetched the audit record; the
  forced path (`--force` / `--refresh-audits`) adds exactly one `wl audit-show`.
- **Children remain exempt** from the flag (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H).
- No new user-facing CLI flags; no change to how a producer clears the flag.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the passing-verdict lifecycle
  (~13576–13600) appends `["--needs-producer-review", "yes"]` for every
  top-level item with no reference to prior review state; the failing-verdict
  lifecycle (~13626–13660) adds the same flag **only** under
  `if ctx.merge_gate_blocker:` in the demotion branch.
- The runner already fetches everything needed for the decision: `wl show` at
  ~10247 yields `ctx.wi` (including `parentId` and `needsProducerReview`), and
  the pre-audit `original_status` / `original_stage` capture (~10238–10256) is
  the natural home for a pre-audit audit-record capture.
- `_check_audit_freshness` (~2085–2160) already runs `wl audit-show <id> --json`
  on the non-forced path and compares the stored v2 content fingerprint with the
  recomputed one — the same data Option B+ needs. The forced path
  (`--force`, `--refresh-audits`, batch drains) bypasses the gate, so an explicit
  capture is required there.
- `audit_results` (ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts` ~305–315) already stores
  `ready_to_close`, `audited_at`, `fingerprint`; `wl audit-show --json` exposes
  `fingerprint` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts`). `wl list --json` additionally
  emits a recomputed `currentFingerprint` via `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`
  (parity-tested against the Python algorithm).
- The audit content fingerprint is **item-data-only** (schema 2: sha256 over
  `title` + `description`) — comments and flag flips do not contribute, so a
  review-clear or a comment cannot invalidate a stored fingerprint.
- ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts` is a flag-only flip; the ship gate's
  remediation guidance (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` ~506–530) and
  `run-release.js` (~668–710) clear flags with `wl update <id>
  --needs-producer-review false`. A durable marker (Option A-lite) would have to
  hook **all** of these, not just `wl reviewed`.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` lives in **ContextHub**, not SorraAgents (the seed's Key
  Files section lists it without a repo; `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
  `skill/audit/SKILL.md` are the SorraAgents-side surfaces).
- The flag-only-flip contract ("flips of `needsProducerReview` do not bump
  `updatedAt`", `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` ~260) means `updatedAt` **cannot** be used
  as a review timestamp — it is bumped by the audit persist itself.
- Current behaviour is pinned by tests that must be updated with the fix:
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (pass-with-hold cases at
  ~239, ~306, ~521, ~544), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` ~436
  (cascade pass still flags), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`
  (fail-flag cases ~523–700).
- The mock harness `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py`
  (`stateful_wl_side_effect`) deliberately passes `audit-show` through untouched
  — it needs a pre-audit audit-record knob so the new rules can be exercised.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

1. **Capture pre-audit audit state** next to the existing pre-audit `wl show`
   capture: `prior_audit = {readyToClose, fingerprint, auditedAt}` (reuse the
   freshness gate's fetch on the non-forced path; one `wl audit-show` otherwise).
   Capture failure ⇒ treat as "no prior audit" (fail-safe → flag).
2. **Add one predicate** (e.g. `_producer_review_preserved(wi, prior_audit)`)
   implementing the chosen signal from the *Review-state signal* section, with a
   single documented truth table. Pure function, unit-testable without the model.
3. **Passing branch**: keep `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level items
   **unless** the predicate holds, in which case append nothing (preserve the
   stored `false`). Log the decision (stderr + the persisted report line) with the
   reason and fingerprint. The rule is identical for items already at a terminal
   `done` stage (those keep their stage and only gain/lose the flag).
4. **Failing branch (independent `No`)**: emit `--needs-producer-review yes` for
   every top-level `No` verdict — merge-gate-blocked *and* ordinary `No` — keeping
   the existing merge-gate behaviour and adding the general case. Never emit `no`.
   This applies **only** when `_cascade_suppress_demotion` is false (see step 5).
5. **Unchanged branches**: infrastructure-failure restore and cascade-demotion
   suppression keep the flag untouched (no set, no clear) — record this explicitly
   in comments so a future edit does not "helpfully" flag on a timeout or a
   parent-triggered cascade. Per the producer's Q2 answer, a cascade-suppressed
   `No` does **not** flag even when `merge_gate_blocker` is set: the
   `--needs-producer-review yes` must move inside the non-suppressed demotion
   branch (a merge-gate failure that matters is re-surfaced by the next
   independent audit).
6. **Children**: no change (no flag on pass, existing behaviour elsewhere).
7. **Dry-run parity**: `--do-not-persist` still applies the flag rules; the
   persisted-report line is skipped (no report is stored).
8. **Tests** (default suite, `skill/audit/tests/`): extend the mock harness with a
   prior-audit knob, then add the four transition tests (AC5) plus child
   regression, merge-gate parity, the cascade-suppressed-`No`-does-not-flag case
   (Q2), and an "audit-show unavailable ⇒ flagged" fail-safe test.
9. **Docs**: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (add a "Producer-review
   flag lifecycle / content-scoped review" section) and
   `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85 lifecycle text), including the chosen option
   and the fail-safe rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — passing-verdict lifecycle (~13576–13600), failing-verdict lifecycle (~13626–13660), pre-audit capture (~10238–10256), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` (~2085–2230). Needs the pre-audit audit-record capture, the new predicate and both flag rules.
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — report persistence; needs the "Producer review: preserved/required" metadata line (Option B+).
- `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py` — mock harness; needs a prior-audit/`audit-show` knob.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`, `test_audit_runner_review.py`, `test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` — pinned expectations to update plus the new transition tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85) — user-facing lifecycle description.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — implementation reference; new producer-review lifecycle section.
- **Not in scope (Option A-lite, rejected by the producer):** ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts`, `src/commands/reviewed.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`/`migrations/` — no worklog schema or CLI change is made by this item, and no cross-repo dependency is raised.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision 1 (cascade, producer Q2 = no).** A `No` verdict produced by a
  parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item does
  **not** set the flag — the flag follows the demotion: suppressed demotion ⇒ no
  flag. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the item to the producer. Note
  this deliberately narrows the merge-gate branch too: a cascade-suppressed
  merge-gate `No` does not flag (the next independent audit re-surfaces it).
- **Assumption 1 (infrastructure failure).** An infrastructure-failure restore
  leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched (neither set nor cleared): a model
  timeout must never manufacture a producer-review request nor discard a review
  (producer Q3 = yes).
- **Assumption 2 (fail-safe).** Any ambiguity in the review signal resolves to
  *flag* (`yes`), never to *preserve* (`false`).
- **Assumption 3 (scope).** Only the audit runner's lifecycle writes the flag;
  the ship gate's own clearing/escalation paths (`check-audit-gate.js`,
  `check-final-validation.js`, `run-release.js`) are out of scope and unchanged.
- **Risk: derived signal (Option B+).** Without a stored review marker, a
  human cannot see *when* the producer reviewed, only that the flag is `false`
  over an unchanged passing audit. Mitigation: the persisted report line records
  the decision + content fingerprint, and Option B+ upgrades cleanly to Option
  A-lite later.
- **Risk: stale fixture expectations.** The current suite pins the unconditional
  flag in ≥6 places; a rushed edit could "fix" the tests instead of the
  behaviour. Mitigation: each test states which of AC1–AC6 it pins.
- **Risk: extra `wl` latency.** Mitigation: reuse the freshness gate's fetch;
  at most one added `wl audit-show` per forced audit.
- **Accepted edge (Option B+).** A flag cleared by an automated override rather
  than a human (the ship gate's child remediation, or the post-release close
  step) is indistinguishable from a human review. Both are intentional clears and
  preserving them is the correct outcome, so no attempt is made to tell them
  apart.

## Observed

A driven child's `implement.py finish` gate hung for **33 minutes** on one test and was killed by the per-command timeout (2700 s). The pytest process was asleep, not computing (`wchan=hrtimer_nanosleep`, 4 s CPU in 32 min), and its open fds showed which test it was in:

```
lr-x------ 11 -> /tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-0/test_finish_refuses_when_lock_0/main/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock
lr-x------ 12 -> /tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-0/test_finish_refuses_when_lock_0/main/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock
```

The test is `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish`, whose contract is *"a finish against a locked checkout exits non-zero"* — i.e. it must fail fast.

## Root cause

The harness does not neutralise the ambient lock-wait variables, so `phase_finish` honours whatever the caller exported:

- the drive was launched with `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` (needed because a real `finish` must wait for another session's long-held main-checkout lock),
- the test inherits that value and therefore **waits 3 hours** instead of refusing immediately, and
- the gate kills it at `timeoutPerCommand` and reports `reason: timeout` — a red gate whose cause is the test environment, not the change under test.

Any agent (or CI job) that exports `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to make its own `finish` wait turns this test from milliseconds into a multi-hour hang. The same shape applies to every other test that exercises the lock-wait path.

## Impact

- A green change can be reported as a `timeout` gate failure purely because of the caller's environment.
- Long waits poison the whole group run: the run must be repeated with a different environment.
- The symptom is misleading (a hanging test with almost no CPU) and hard to attribute without inspecting `/proc/<pid>/fd`.

## Desired fix (direction)

Make the affected tests environment-hermetic, e.g. an autouse fixture (or the `_finish_harness`) that pins `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`/`IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to `0` via `monkeypatch.setenv`/`delenv` for the duration of the test, and a comment saying why (the wait value is a caller policy, never a test input). Audit every test that reaches the lock-wait path the same way, and add a guard that fails if a test reads a wait timeout inherited from the ambient environment.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] `pytest skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` passes in under a few seconds with `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600` exported.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the refusal path is reached without sleeping (e.g. patches the clock/wait and asserts it was never entered, or asserts elapsed < N seconds).
- [ ] The same hermeticity is applied to any other test that exercises `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / test-slot waits.

# audit skill: AC extraction rejects qualified `Acceptance Criteria` headings

**Symptom (observed auditing RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L, 2026-11-01):** `audit_runner.py issue` returned `Ready to close: No` with `No acceptance criteria defined.` and **0 model calls**, then demoted the item to `open`/`plan_complete` — even though the item's description carries three numbered acceptance criteria under the heading `## Acceptance criteria for this project`.

## Root cause

`_extract_acs()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` matches the AC heading with an anchored regex:

```
^(?:Acceptance|Success)\s+Criteria:?\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*$
```

The match is applied to the line **after** `_normalize_heading_line()` strips markdown heading markers — but a trailing qualifier such as `for this project` is not allowed (only an optional colon or parenthetical is), so the heading never matches and the function returns the `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` sentinel. The pipeline then treats that sentinel as the AC body (a `warning` verdict), skips Phase 2, and produces a `No` verdict which demotes the item.

## Consequences

- A valid, auditable item audits as if it has no ACs: Phase 1 and Phase 2 screening are skipped (0 pi calls), and the item is demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` on the normal `No` path.
- The failure is silent to the model — no prompt ever sees the AC list, so no evidence names the extraction failure.

## Reproduction

`audit_runner.py issue` against an item whose description AC-section heading carries a trailing qualifier, e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project` (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L exhibited this; its three criteria were manually verified satisfied, and the heading had to be normalised to `## Acceptance Criteria` before the audit would screen them).

## Suggested fix

Relax the heading pattern to accept trailing free text while keeping canonical headings byte-compatible: e.g. match `Acceptance Criteria` / `Success Criteria` optionally followed by `:`, a parenthetical, a trailing qualifier (`for …`), or end-of-line. Add regression tests covering heading variants: canonical, lowercase `c`, colon, parenthetical, and a trailing-qualifier heading.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_extract_acs()` (or the heading matcher it uses) recognises AC headings with a trailing qualifier (e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project`), extracting the numbered/bulleted items below them.
2. Canonical headings (`## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Success Criteria`, optional colon/parenthetical) behave unchanged — no regression.
3. A unit test covers the exact qualifier variant from the RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L reproduction.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_extract_acs`, `_normalize_heading_line`)

# Reduce implement skill cold-start context (regressed ~5× since F5 trim)

## Problem statement

The implement skill starts with a very large context. Measured across real
sessions, a **cold** `/skill:implement` turn is ~24–25k tokens at the 50th
percentile — dominated (~78%) by the skill's own `SKILL.md` body, which is
inlined verbatim into the user message on every invocation. This sits right at
the edge of local acceptance: the near-miss population clusters just above the
38,000 cold threshold (38,298–38,752), and resumed/hydrated sessions blow past
it entirely (216k–452k). Every additional byte of `SKILL.md` inflates *every*
implement turn, not just edge cases.

## Root cause (measured)

1. **`skill/implement/SKILL.md` re-bloated ~5× since the F5 trim.**
   - F5 (SA-0MSLK7SAE0032V9K, 2026-08-10) trimmed it to **15,447 B** with a
     stated budget of ≤15,453 B.
   - It is now **76,286 B / 75,774 chars (≈19k tokens)** — **4.9× over the F5
     budget**.
   - Growth was gradual: each of the ~67 subsequent commits appended new
     feature-card prose back into the brief instead of the reference doc
     (largest single-commit deltas: +6.6k B SA-0MVPZGAU5001FDO3, +4.1k B
     80dbf5a23 stash-hygiene, +3.1k B 19db86445 gate-failure docs, +3.0k B
     a624d18ed outbound-edge gate, +2.1k B each drive and per-child lock).
2. **The largest inline blocks are deep reference material, not operational
   steps.** The `## Steps` section alone is 45.5k chars (~11.4k tok):
   - `6.1 Parent recursion` — **19,068 chars (~4.8k tok)** — drive/parent
     orchestration, per-child locks, failure-recovery tiers, guard tables
   - `9. Commit, Push and mark in_review` — **11,079 chars (~2.8k tok)** —
     push timeout, terminal-status read-back, gate-failure reason tables
   - `### When finish refuses` — **7,202 chars (~1.8k tok)**
   - Background Job Etiquette — 3,927 chars; StatusLifecycle Integration —
     2,785 chars; gate-failure `reason`/facts — 3,142 chars
3. **The deep detail already lives in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
   (82,844 B) but the SKILL.md body duplicates it inline** instead of linking
   to it. The F5 "operational brief + deep docs" pattern was abandoned.
4. **No regression gate exists on SKILL.md *body* size.** The context-budget
   gate (`measure_context.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, tests
   `test_context_budget_gate.py`) only measures AGENTS.md files and the
   skills-section *description prose* (`skills_prose` = frontmatter
   `description:`), **not** the `SKILL.md` bodies loaded on invocation. The F5
   budget was a one-shot trim with no ongoing enforcement, so the file could
   silently regrow.
5. **Secondary: the system prompt contributes ~5.3k tokens** (measured 21,080
   chars in a real session) — dominated by `project_context` (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md
   ~3.2k tok + project AGENTS.md). Projects with very large AGENTS.md (e.g.
   AI_Hell system sections = 45,416 chars ≈ 11.3k tok) push near-miss sessions
   over the threshold without any skill change.
6. **The 216k–452k sessions are a separate failure mode** — resumed/hydrated
   sessions where the implement turn arrived after a huge *accumulated*
   context (the tables mark them as such). Not caused by SKILL.md alone, but a
   small SKILL.md body reduces the burn rate toward that failure.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — runs `/skill:implement` on work items; the local
  proxy must accept the turn's context. A 25k baseline with near-miss at 38k
  is too close to the edge and growing (sessions already exceed 200–450k).
- **Agents** — every implement turn pays the fixed ~19k-token cost of the
  SKILL.md body before doing any work; a smaller brief loads faster and leaves
  more headroom for the work itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` is reduced to **≤ 20,000 B** (measurable with
   `wc -c`), a ≥74% cut from the current 76,286 B, restoring the F5
   "operational brief" size class (F5 budget was ≤15,453 B).
2. Every removed/abridged section is preserved — verbatim or summarised with a
   link + SA reference — in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (or an
   appendix there), so no behavioural content is lost (F5 AC2 pattern).
3. The brief still documents every command/flag an operator needs to run the
   workflow end-to-end (worktree creation, `implement.py start/finish/parent/
   drive`, `wl` status transitions, StatusLifecycle, push-to-dev); workflow
   semantics are unchanged.
4. A **regression gate on SKILL.md body size** is added so the file cannot
   silently regrow: extend `measure_context.py` (or the context-budget gate /
   a dedicated test) with a `skill_implement_md` byte threshold committed in
   `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, enforced by the pre-push hook
   and a test — mirroring how AGENTS.md sizes are already gated.
5. Tests asserting SKILL.md content are updated and passing:
   `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_tdd.py`, `skill/implement/tests/` etc. — content that
   moved to the reference doc must be asserted against the reference doc
   (F5 AC4 pattern: "SKILL.md-content tests updated to check the reference
   docs").

   a cold implement turn at ≤ ~6.5k tokens from the skill body (down from

  moved prose must be repointed to the reference doc, not deleted.
- Keep the hidden-skill invocation map and extension conventions intact
  (`extension.json`, `SKILL_PREFIX/POSTFIX.md`).
- No change to `implement.py` runtime behaviour — this is a documentation/

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — 82,844 B, already holds deep

- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` + `context-budget.thresholds.json` — startup

- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — the canonical measurer;

  creation detail) to `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, leaving a

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — destination for relocated deep

  `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_tdd.py`,

  path (client-side compaction disabled) — relevant to the giant 200k–452k
  hydrated-session failure mode, tracked separately, not fixed here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** the same bloat affects other skills (audit 64.1 KB, ship
  33.8 KB, plan 27.2 KB, intake 21.5 KB, test 20.4 KB). This item is scoped to
  implement only; sibling trims should be separate work items. Risk: an
  operator may expect all skills trimmed at once — the ACs pin implement only.
- **Regression gate ≠ guarantee:** a body-size gate prevents silent regrowth
  but every *intentional* addition must flow through the gate (regenerate
  thresholds with justification, as AGENTS.md bumps do). Decide one
  threshold: F5-budget (15,453 B) vs "brief" allowance (20 KB) — AC1 proposes
  20 KB with F5 as reference. (Choose 20,000 B — see AC1; can be lowered after
  acceptance to the exact F5 figure if the brief compresses further.)
- **Resumed/hydrated giants (216k–452k):** not fully fixable by SKILL.md size

  intentionally exclude this; a smaller body reduces burn rate toward it but a
  separate work item may be needed for session-hydration limits.
- **Content-pinning tests:** some tests assert exact prose in SKILL.md; the
  almost-verbatim overlap check found ~0% shared lines with the reference doc,
  so moved prose will need deliberate re-pinning in tests — budget for it.
- **Assumption:** a ~19k-token body is the primary lever (78% of a 24.2k cold
  turn; 4.9× over the F5 budget) — verified by direct measurement of the file
  and real session logs on this machine.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metric defines the problem — P50 cold-start tokens, the 38k
  near-miss threshold, or the 200k–452k hydrated sessions?" — Answer
  (operator, seed context): "At P50 we are around 25k which is right on the
  edge of what can be accepted locally. We need to get this down." The 5
  largest sessions are explicitly "resumed/hydrated — the implement turn
  arrived after a huge accumulated context"; the 38k cluster is the
  near-miss population. Source: intake seed + session tables (2026-11-01).
  Research: verified cold-turn composition = SKILL.md body (~19k tok) +
  system sections (~5.3k tok) ≈ 24.2k, matching P50 ≈ 25k. The giant-session
  mode is a separate failure tracked in Risks.
- Q: "Is a regression gate (AC4) in scope, or just the trim?" — Answer
  (intake inference from F5/F6 precedent + 'get this down'): a gate is
  required — without it the F5 trim (which had a budget that was never
  enforced) simply repeats. Marked AC4; if the operator wants the trim only,
  AC4 can be dropped without weakening ACs 1–3/5–7. OPEN QUESTION: confirm
  the 20,000 B allowance vs the exact F5 15,453 B figure.

# A no-op finish finalised an item whose acceptance criteria were unmet

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` marks a work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal) even
when its worktree produced **no commit attributable to the item** and its
acceptance criteria were never exercised (e.g. an operational run that must
happen on its own schedule). On that no-op path the report attributes the
ambient `dev` HEAD — a hash belonging to a *different* work item — as "the
commit", so a parent whose child carries zero work is advanced to `in_review`:
a silent false positive that hides unmet ACs from the producer and the audit
skill.

## Users

- **Driven child sessions / agents**: a session whose worktree is clean
  (first session died before writing, or the item legitimately waits on an
  external window) must never see its item silently finalised with no work.
- **Producers / operators**: must be able to trust `in_review` — it means the
  ACs are actually met. A false `in_review` hides outstanding criteria.
- **Audit skill**: reads terminal state to decide what to verify; a false
  terminal hides a genuinely unmet AC5-style operational criterion.
- **Verification-only items** (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): items whose only
  deliverable is *running* a measurement and recording evidence — the
  legitimate no-op-push path must keep working, now behind an explicit signal.

### User stories

- As a producer, when a child was finalised with zero commits and no
  acceptance evidence, I want the item to stay open with a loud explanation,
  so `in_review` never hides unmet ACs (the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM cascade is
  impossible).
- As an agent running `finish`, when I legitimately complete a
  verification-only item with no code change, I want an explicit
  `--verification-only` flag that finalises it and reports "no changes, no
  commit" — never a commit hash belonging to someone else's work.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — No-op finish refuses the terminal write by default.** When
  `phase_finish` detects its worktree produced no commit attributable to the
  item (clean-tree/no-diff path) and no `--verification-only` signal is
  present, it must **not** write `status=completed`/`stage=in_review`: the
  item stays in its prior state, `finish` fails (or reports loudly) with an
  actionable message, and no "Implementation complete. Commit \<sha\>" comment
  is posted using an ambient/unrelated HEAD.
- **AC2 — Commit attribution is never false.** `finish`'s completion report
  may only name a commit that is attributable to this item (created by this
  finish run or a prior run of this item's worktree). On the no-commit path it
  must say "no changes / no commit", naming the retained worktree and any
  recorded evidence instead of the ambient `dev` HEAD.
- **AC3 — Verification-only path preserved behind an explicit flag.** An
  explicit opt-in (e.g. `implement.py finish <id> --verification-only`) still
  finalises a no-commit item to `completed`/`in_review`, exactly preserving
  the behaviour pinned by `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`
  (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): terminal status persists and the store read-back
  assertion still passes, but the report names "no changes" and never
  misattributes a hash.
- **AC4 — drive/phase_parent never presents zero work as finishable.** A child
  whose worktree exists but carries no commit attributable to the item and no
  verification-only signal is classified as "no work / not finalisable":
  `drive`/`phase_parent` does **not** run `finish` on it, reports it as such
  (child stays open), and the parent is **not** advanced to `in_review`.
  Finish's own refusal (AC1) remains the defence in depth for direct
  invocation.
- **AC5 — Automated regression coverage.** Unit/integration tests cover:
  (i) commit-vs-no-op distinction in `git_commit`, (ii) the default refusal
  path (AC1), (iii) the `--verification-only` path (AC3) including the
  existing no-diff status regression pin, and (iv) the drive/phase_parent
  classification (AC4).
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (and any related
  implement-skill docs) documents the new no-op semantics, the
  `--verification-only` flag, and how the agent should treat a clean,
  commit-less worktree.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Preserve the deliberate no-op-push path** (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): the
  regression pin `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` must
  continue to pass — verification-only items must remain finalisable, now only
  via the explicit signal (per the producer's decision).
- **Lifecycle invariants unchanged**: `StatusLifecycle` remains the only
  writer of status/stage; assignee release on completion is unchanged; the
  terminal read-back assertion (`_assert_terminal_status`) stays as the
  fail-loud guard.
- **Deterministic, machine-checkable gating**: no free-text/heuristic evidence
  parsing as the gate for the no-op path — an explicit flag carries it
  (producer decision Q2).
- **Surgical change**: no new flags or behaviour outside `implement.py finish`
  and `drive`/`phase_parent` classification unless required by the ACs.

## Existing state

- `git_commit` (lines ~2961) returns `True` both when it commits and when the
  tree is clean ("No changes to commit (clean working tree)"), so
  `phase_finish` cannot distinguish a real commit from a no-op.
- After `git_commit`, `phase_finish` reads `git_get_commit_hash(worktree_path)`
  (the branch HEAD — for a clean, commit-less worktree this is the ambient
  `dev` HEAD, i.e. someone else's commit), pushes the identical branch as a
  no-op, and `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes
  `status=completed`/`stage=in_review`. The completion comment reports
  "Implementation complete. Commit: \<ambient HEAD\>".
- `_assert_terminal_status` (lines ~707) only verifies the store *held* the
  terminal write — it cannot distinguish "finished work" from "nothing to do".
- `drive`/`phase_parent` (lines ~9240–9320) run `finish` whenever
  `_has_worktree_changes` is truthy; a clean-but-present worktree is reported
  as "worktree exists … implement, then re-run", but the no-op finish path
  above still finalises a commit-less child when it is reached (observed
  2026-11-01T12:55Z).
- The observed incident: `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1` was flipped
  completed/in_review with zero work; its parent `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` was
  consequently advanced to in_review with AC5 genuinely unmet. Correction was
  applied manually ("Reopened — AC5 measurement was never run (spurious
  finalisation)").

## Desired change

- `git_commit` reports whether a commit was actually created (structured
  result / distinct signal), so `phase_finish` can detect the no-op path
  before the push.
- On the no-op path **without** `--verification-only`: abort before the
  terminal write — item stays open, finish fails loudly with an actionable
  message naming the retained worktree and why, no misattributed commit hash.
- On the no-op path **with** `--verification-only`: finalise as today
  (preserving OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58), but report "no changes / no commit"
  instead of an ambient HEAD.
- `drive`/`phase_parent`: classify a child whose worktree has no attributable
  commit and no verification-only signal as "no work / not finalisable" —
  report and leave open so the parent never advances; keep finish's refusal
  as defence in depth.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_commit` (~2961) commit-vs-no-op
  signal; `git_get_commit_hash` (~3213) attribution; `phase_finish` (~7454)
  refusal + `--verification-only` gating + completion comment wording;
  `_assert_terminal_status` (~707) no-op-path wording; `drive`/`phase_parent`
  (`_classify_child` ~1423, `_has_worktree_changes` ~8798, `_git_path_has_changes`
  ~12099, the drive loop ~9240) classification + reporting.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — existing regression
  pin for the no-op terminal transition; update to assert the gated path and
  add the refusal-path tests.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document `--verification-only` and the no-op
  refusal semantics.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` CLI arg parsing (~12175–12360) — add
  the `--verification-only` flag.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVXU5YWQ004YGZS` — originating work item (this bug, recorded in the llm
  project worklog; moved here because the implement skill source lives in this
  repo).
- `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1`, `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` — the child falsely finalised
  and the parent wrongly advanced to in_review (observed evidence).
- `OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58` — the deliberate no-op-push path for verification-only
  items; its behaviour must be preserved behind the explicit flag.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — regression pin for
  OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58 (terminal status persists on the no-op path).
- Related llm-project items on finish's push/gate correctness (different
  defect surfaces, same file): `LP-0MVTJ2B3H00258U1`, `LP-0MVWY2XQ8005JL0S`,
  `LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0`.
- `SA-0MS8XDUFK004AZ5V` Remove accidentally-tracked .implement_state.json from
  dev — the tracked state file can make a commit-less worktree read as "has
  changes", feeding the false finish; related by find_related.
- `SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV` Reconcile terminal child once finish bound exhausted —
  adjacent drive/finish lifecycle reconciliation; related by find_related.
- `SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG` Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull —
  implement-skill maintenance task; related by find_related.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** tightening `finish` could block a legitimate no-op finalise that an
  operator performs directly (without the flag). Mitigation: the refusal
  message names the exact flag/recovery steps, and the manual-push style
  recovery comment mirrors existing finish failure paths.
- **Risk:** `drive` no longer running finish on a "no work" child could strand
  a genuinely complete-but-uncommitted child. Mitigation: the classifier
  checks for dirty files *and* commits ahead (existing `_git_path_has_changes`
  semantics) and reports the child as "not finalisable" with the worktree
  path, so an agent re-enters and finishes it properly.
- **Assumption:** acceptance *evidence* (prose comments citing operational
  runs) is not a machine-checkable gate; the explicit flag is the gate, and
  evidence stays advisory (producer decision Q2).
- **Scope-creep risk:** follow-ups observed during implementation (e.g.
  reconciling `drive` messaging, flag naming) are recorded as separate linked
  work items, not folded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Default outcome of a no-op finish with no commit attributable to the
  item?" — Answer (producer): **(a) Refuse the terminal write** — finish fails
  loudly, item stays open, finalise requires explicit opt-in. Source:
  interactive reply 2026-11-02. **Recommended: (a)**.
- Q2: "What gates legitimate finalisation of a no-commit item
  (verification-only)? (a) explicit CLI flag; (b) recorded acceptance evidence;
  (c) both." — Answer (producer): **(a) explicit CLI flag** (e.g.
  `--verification-only`), no content heuristics. Source: interactive reply
  2026-11-02. **Recommended: (a)**. Research: evidence comments are prose and
  weak as a hard gate; a flag is deterministic and machine-checkable
  (confirmable in `finish`'s report and tests).
- Q3: "drive/phase_parent treatment of a child whose worktree exists but has
  no commit and no finalise signal? (a) classify 'no work / not finalisable' —
  never run finish, keep open so the parent never advances; (b) keep current
  classification, rely on finish's refusal; (c) auto-detect and re-queue."
  — Answer (producer): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-02.
  **Recommended: (a)** — kills the cascade at the source, with finish's own
  refusal as defence in depth for direct invocations.

Research & evidence (agent):
- Traced the no-op path in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `git_commit`
  returns `True` on a clean tree; `git_get_commit_hash` reports the branch HEAD
  (ambient dev HEAD); no-op push; `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes the
  terminal transition.
- Read `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`: the deliberate
  no-op terminal transition is pinned (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58); tests stub
  `git_commit` green and do not distinguish committed vs nothing-to-commit.
- Verified the installed implement skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`) is a
  byte-identical copy of this repo's `skill/implement/` — this repo is the
  source of truth, hence the item lives here.

# audit: gap-mapped children re-screen in-main-slot and overwrite serviced child audits

## Observed on SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB (epic, all 10 children terminal and on dev)

An epic audit whose **parent** carries one `partial` AC cannot converge while the
default in-main-slot child-audit mode is active. Every run re-screens the same
gap-mapped children, re-blocks on the pending-screens gate, and (worse) overwrites
child audits that a previous session had serviced with real verdicts.

## Root cause (two interacting behaviours)

1. **Gap-mapped children ignore their stored verdict.** In the default
   parent-first flow (`_phase_children`, `audit_children=False`) the
   `not parent_gaps` branch consults `_child_content_changed()` (content-gated
   reuse), but the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch appends the child
   to `pending_children` **without** consulting its stored audit — unlike the
   `--audit-children` P7 pre-pass, which reuses a fresh stored child audit via
   `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and never re-screens it.
2. **In-main-slot mode cannot service screens inside the run.** With
   `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` (default `true`) the gap-mapped child screens are
   emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` and the child audits are persisted as
   `partial` + `main-session review`. A later `persist` pass then **overwrites**
   the previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit with that pending
   `partial` report.

Net effect: service the screens → re-run the parent → the children are re-screened
and their good audits are destroyed → the parent still reports
`Ready to close: No` with `Child screens pending`. The
`<id>.pending-screens.json` signal is never cleared.

## Evidence (this item's run)

| Step | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Audit run 1 | 08:13 | `Ready to close: No`, 7 in-main-slot screens emitted |
| Screens serviced by the session (real file:line evidence) | ~09:55 | 6 children `Yes`, 1 `No` (documented downstream AC) |
| Audit re-run (`--force`, because the stored report was content-fresh) | 10:04 | 14 screens re-emitted; **all 7 child audits overwritten back to `partial` + `main-session review`**; parent `No` with 7 pending screens |
| Screens re-serviced by hand (again) | 10:20 | 6 `Yes` / 1 `No` restored |

The parent's single blocking AC (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB AC10) is a downstream
verification owned by a **different repository** (`LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X`), so it can
never become `met` on this host — the loop is permanent, not a transient state.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow, a
  gap-mapped child with a content-fresh stored audit is reused (its persisted AC
  verdicts adopted, exactly as the `--audit-children` pre-pass does) and is NOT
  added to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run never persists a
  pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and
  carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** With all children terminal and only one unsatisfiable
  parent AC, a re-run after servicing the child screens reports
  `Ready to close: No` naming **that AC only** (no `Child screens pending` gate),
  and the pending-screens signal is cleared.
- **AC4 — Regression tests** cover both flows (gap-mapped reuse, no overwrite on
  persist) with no real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this (discovered-from).
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling
  (mitigates the reporting side only; it does not stop the re-screen/overwrite).
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — the cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent
  permanently `partial` on this host.

## Problem

Every `audit_runner.py issue <id>` run that finds a medium/low code-quality finding it classifies as a *candidate false positive*:

1. creates a **new** chore work item (`ruff BLE001 in .../implement.py — candidate false positive — producer decision required`), and
2. sets `needsProducerReview = true` on the audited parent item.

Observed during the 2026-11-02 release prep: a backlog of 20+ such chore items accumulated (SA-0MVBD5ZBD007HQZA, SA-0MVI2ZZH9004WGIG, SA-0MVZIKFES006HD99, SA-0MVZK9SBF000HLS2, SA-0MVZL5TE1007YTVJ, SA-0MVZL69QA0007CRJ, ...), and **7 of 36 in_review items** were blocked by the ship skill's producer-review gate purely because of them. Clearing the flag is a manual `wl update` per item and the next audit re-creates another chore + flag, so a release can never converge.

## Expected

- A false-positive candidate should be recorded **once** (deduplicated by rule + file + line + fingerprint), not once per audit run.
- A passing audit verdict (`readyToClose === true`) should clear / not set `needsProducerReview`; the flag should reflect a genuine producer decision, not the existence of an unresolved low-severity lint candidate.
- Consider a documented producer-level suppression (e.g. a per-rule/file allowlist, or an `auditWaiver`) so accepted false positives stop re-surfacing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeated audits of the same unchanged item do not create duplicate chore items (dedupe proven by a test).
2. An audit that ends `Ready to close: Yes` leaves `needsProducerReview` false.
3. An accepted false positive can be recorded once (suppression/waiver) and no longer re-flags the parent.
4. Release gate regression test: a repository with N accepted false-positive chores does not fail the ship producer-review gate.
5. Full suite green.

## Impact

Blocks `/skill:ship release` on repositories with deliberate lint patterns; each release needs manual flag clearing (2026-11-02 release: 7 items cleared by hand).

## Problem

`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (added in v0.1.25) builds a fixture release repo and drives `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` with a stubbed suite runner. Under a clean shell the module is green (verified: `run_tests.py --scope full --force` at tree a9b008ead → 5820 passed). Under the **pre-push hook** (i.e. any push to `dev`/`main`) the same three tests fail:

```
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestGreenGate::test_green_gate_invokes_full_scope_and_release_proceeds
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestRedGate::test_red_gate_blocks_release_before_pr
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestMissingRunnerFailClosed::test_missing_runner_fails_closed
FileNotFoundError: .../runner-marker.txt   (the stubbed runner was never invoked)
```

Root cause: git exports `GIT_DIR` (and the suite gate may export `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) into hook environments; the fixture repo's git commands then resolve against the *live* checkout instead of the fixture, so `merge-dev-to-main.sh` short-circuits and the suite gate never runs. This is the same class as SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX (node fixtures inheriting the finish gate's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`).

**Consequence:** the pre-push full-suite gate is red for every `dev` push, so `dev` cannot be synced with `main` after a release (hit during the 2026-11-02 v0.1.25 release; the sync required `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` with a separately verified green tree).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` scrubs the ambient git environment (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or equivalent) for both the fixture repo construction and the merge-script subprocess, so it passes when run from a git hook.
2. A regression test proves the module passes with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the live repository.
3. `git push origin dev` (fast-forward) succeeds without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` after the fix.
4. Full suite green in both a clean shell and a hook-like environment.

## Related

- SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX — same leak class for node fixtures.
- SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42 — audit/producer-review churn (unrelated, same release session).

## Problem statement

The paid MunitoAI DeepSeek configuration lives only in the tracked
`.pi-config/agent` files and in this machine's `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, because
`scripts/install_pi.sh` merely copies those files **when the destination does not
already exist** — any established machine keeps its own (possibly drifted)
`models.json` and never receives the MunitoAI provider. The newer paid model
`deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is not configured at all, and no
DeepSeek/MunitoAI entry is in `enabledModels`, so paid DeepSeek cannot be reached
from the model cycle.

## Users

Framework operator (producer) on any machine that installs SorraAgents, and any
agent session that wants to run a paid DeepSeek model.

- As an operator, I want `scripts/install_pi.sh` to apply the tracked MunitoAI
  paid-DeepSeek provider to `~/.pi/agent/models.json` even when that file already
  exists, so every project on every machine gets the same model set without me
  hand-editing JSON.
- As an operator, I want the paid DeepSeek models in `enabledModels`, so I can
  reach them with `Ctrl+P` model cycling and as a startup selection.
- As an agent session, I want to select
  `MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` and have it answer, so paid
  DeepSeek is usable for real work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/models.json` exposes **both** paid MunitoAI DeepSeek
  models under one `MunitoAI` provider — `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`
  (existing) and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (new) — with
  `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`; no credential is committed.
- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` `enabledModels` contains `MunitoAI/*` and
  `deepseek/deepseek*` in addition to the existing `Local Proxy/plan` and
  `Local Proxy/code` entries.
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` merges the tracked `providers` (models and
  `modelOverrides` included) into an existing `~/.pi/agent/models.json` and
  unions the tracked `enabledModels` into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, instead

## Problem statement

The audit pipeline currently treats *any* failing test as a failure of the audit: a red F3 auto-execution leaves execution-dependent ACs `partial` (so `Ready to close: No`), and a red merge-gate suite run fails the integration closed. That is the right behaviour for the release gate, but it is wrong for the everyday audits an agent runs while implementing a work item: unrelated, pre-existing red unit tests (e.g. another item's broken test) block an otherwise complete item and send the audit into a remediation loop that cannot succeed.

Audits must therefore support two test-failure modes: **strict** (today's behaviour — any failing test fails the audit) and **permissive** (a failing **unit** test that is provably *not affected in any way* by the audited work item's changes does not fail the audit; integration/end-to-end failures always fail).

## Users

- **Agent implementing a work item** — "As an agent running `/skill:audit` on my in-progress item, I want an unrelated red unit test elsewhere in the repo not to block my item, so that I do not chase failures outside my change set."
- **Release engineer (ship skill)** — "As the release gate, I want every audited item to have a genuinely green suite, so that `dev` is never promoted to `main` on the back of excused failures."
- **Producer reviewing an audit** — "As a reviewer, I want the persisted audit report to state which mode was used and, for every excused failure, the evidence that it was unrelated, so that I can trust a permissive pass."

Example user stories:

- Permissive: `tests/test_other_skill.py::test_unrelated` fails; the item only touched `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`; the audit still returns `Ready to close: Yes` with the failure listed as excused (unrelated, unit) and a critical `test-failure` work item created.
- Strict: the same failure blocks the audit; ship re-runs the item under `--strict` and refuses to release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mode resolution and default.** `audit_runner.py issue` (and `batch`) accepts `--strict` / `--no-strict`, with `AUDIT_STRICT=1` as the environment equivalent; **the default is permissive**. Precedence is flag > env > default, resolved once and recorded. Unit tests cover the precedence matrix and that `--strict` reproduces today's verdict for a red suite (any failure ⇒ `Ready to close: No`).
2. **Permissive excusal — unrelated unit failures.** In permissive mode, a red suite whose failures are **all** unit-classified **and** proven unrelated to the item's changes does not fail the audit: the runner injects a "run red, excused failures" evidence block into the Phase 1/Phase 2 prompts (so execution-dependent ACs may be marked `met`), the report gains a `## Test Failure Mode` section listing every excused failure with its classification and relatedness evidence, and the `--json` payload carries the same data. Unit tests cover the excused path end-to-end at the verdict level.
3. **Permissive fail-closed cases.** In permissive mode the audit still fails when (a) any failure is integration/end-to-end classified, (b) any unit failure is affected by the item's changes, or (c) relatedness is inconclusive and no baseline comparison can be performed. Unit tests cover each case individually, plus the mixed case (one excusable + one blocking failure ⇒ audit fails).
4. **Scope classification and relatedness algorithm.** Failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.
5. **Triage is preserved.** Excused failures are still triaged into critical `test-failure` work items (same dedup + cap semantics as today). Unit tests assert triage is invoked for excused failures as well as blocking ones.
6. **Ship uses strict mode.** All three ship audit call sites (`check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`, `refresh-audits.js`) pass `--strict`, and the manual remediation commands they surface include `--strict`. Tests assert the constructed command strings; the flag name is generic (`--strict`, not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness checks can share it.
7. **Freshness respects mode strength.** A strict run must never reuse a stored permissive "Yes" (it re-runs); a permissive run may reuse a stored strict "Yes". Unit tests cover both directions.
8. **Documentation and validation.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document both modes, the flag/env precedence, the classification and relatedness rules, and which callers use which mode. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only mandate:** the audit stays read-only except for the existing sanctioned exceptions. The baseline comparison runs only the failing tests, in a scratch worktree (never the main checkout), through the existing paced runner (`run_tests.paced_runner()`) and under the existing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down so nested suite runs cannot recurse.
- **Strict mode must be byte-for-byte today's behaviour** — no verdict change for existing strict callers.
- **Never-block guarantee (F4) is preserved:** the mode never introduces a hard exit for infrastructure failure; inability to classify or baseline degrades to *affected* (fail closed on the verdict), never a crash.
- **The dev-push pre-push full-suite gate is unchanged** — permissive mode does not weaken it; it only governs the audit verdict.
- **Determinism:** the excusal decision must be reproducible from the persisted report alone (mode, classification, mapping/baseline evidence recorded).
- **No new suite executions on the happy path:** a green suite behaves exactly as today; excusal work happens only when the suite is red.
- Scope-creep guard: any richer relatedness heuristic (e.g. coverage-based mapping), or per-repo `unitTestGlobs`/`integrationTestGlobs` configuration, is out of scope — record it as a linked follow-up if it turns out to be needed.

## Existing state

- `_run_tests_via_test_skill()` (F3 auto-execution) parses failures, triages them, and returns `success`; a red run injects **no** GREEN-RUN block, so execution-dependent ACs stay `partial` ⇒ `Ready to close: No`. Red cached entries (`_classify_full_suite_cache` → `red`) also stay partial with no execution.
- `_integrate_into_dev()` (Phase 1 merge gate) runs `run_suite("all")`; `success == False` ⇒ `Integration failed: test suite failed.` ⇒ audit fails closed.
- Green evidence reaches the parent Phase-1 screen, both child Phase-1 screens and every Phase 2 prompt (`_green_run_prompt_block`, `_auto_green_run_prompt_block`, `_test_skill_run_prompt_block`).
- The freshness gate fingerprints `{title_hash, description_hash}` only — it has no notion of *how* a verdict was produced, so a permissive "Yes" would currently satisfy ship's strict re-run.
- Item changed-file resolution already exists (`_resolve_touched_files`, `_extract_key_files`); failure parsing exists (`parse_pytest_failures`, `parse_node_failures`); suite resolution exists (`full_suite_commands`).
- Ship invokes the runner from `check-audit-gate.js:841`, `check-final-validation.js:479`, `refresh-audits.js:131` (`runAuditCommand` defaults), plus the surfaced manual commands in `check-audit-gate.js:386/518/638` and `audit-remediation.js:43`.
- `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers; the repo has no `integration`/`e2e` markers, and `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists — path convention is the practical classifier.

## Desired change

**Headline:** add a `--strict` audit mode (permissive by default) in which only *unrelated unit* failures are excused, and make the ship release gate audit strictly.

1. **Mode plumbing.** New `--strict` / `--no-strict` flags on `issue` and `batch`, `AUDIT_STRICT` env var, default permissive; a resolved `strict: bool` on `_AuditContext`, threaded to the F3 path, the merge gate, the prompt evidence builders, the report assembler and the `--json` payload.
2. **Failure classification + relatedness module** (helpers in `audit_runner.py`):
   - `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` → `"unit"` | `"integration"` from the path-pattern table (fail closed to `integration`).
   - `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` → `"affected"` | `"unrelated"` | `"inconclusive"` (test file match, import scan against changed modules, shared test-infrastructure match).
   - `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` → per-failure verdicts by re-running only the inconclusive failures in a scratch worktree at the pre-change commit.
3. **Verdict integration.** A single helper (e.g. `_evaluate_red_suite(...)`) that, in strict mode, returns "blocked" for any failure, and in permissive mode returns `blocked` (with reasons) or `excused` (with per-failure evidence). Both the F3 path and the merge gate consume it. Excused-red injects an evidence block analogous to the GREEN-RUN blocks; blocked-red keeps today's behaviour and diagnostics.
4. **Cached-red handling (consistency).** In permissive mode a `red` cached full-suite entry is classified from the cached output (already stored) rather than being accepted as blocking-by-default; if the cached output yields no parseable failure records the runner executes the suite as it does on a miss. Strict mode keeps today's cached-red behaviour unchanged.
5. **Persistence and report.** `## Test Failure Mode` section (mode, resolution source, per-failure classification/relatedness/evidence, baseline commit used); `--json` payload key `test_failure_mode`; the mode is part of the stored audit so the freshness gate can compare mode strength (strict re-runs over permissive; permissive may reuse strict).
6. **Ship wiring.** `--strict` added to the three ship runner invocations and the surfaced manual remediation commands.
7. **Docs.** Audit + ship SKILL files and their `docs/dev/*-reference.md` companions updated with the contract, the default, and the caller matrix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — mode resolution/plumbing; `_classify_test_failure_scope`, `_failure_relatedness`, `_baseline_unrelated`, `_evaluate_red_suite`; excused-red evidence block; `_run_tests_via_test_skill` and `_integrate_into_dev` integration; report + `--json` sections; freshness mode-strength comparison.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document both modes, the `--strict`/`AUDIT_STRICT` precedence, default, classification/relatedness rules, caller matrix.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — full contract: pattern table, relatedness algorithm, baseline worktree rules, cached-red behaviour, mode-strength freshness.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `runAuditCommand` default + surfaced manual commands gain `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — `runAuditCommand` default gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — pre-flight refresh `runAuditCommand` gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — state that ship audits strictly.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_strict_mode.py` (new) — mode precedence, classification table, relatedness mapping, baseline comparison, excused/blocked verdicts, triage-on-excusal, cached-red behaviour, freshness mode strength.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — extend existing F3/merge-gate coverage for the strict path parity.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_audit_strict_flag.mjs` (new) — command-string assertions for the three ship call sites.
- `command/audit.md` — note that the default is permissive and `--strict` is available (optional, if the prompt enumerates flags).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: excusal hides a real regression.** Mitigated by fail-closed defaults (integration always fails; affected or inconclusive always fails) and by recording per-failure evidence in the persisted report.
- **Risk: baseline worktree cost/instability** (merge-base unresolvable, worktree add failure, test absent at baseline). Mitigated: baseline runs only the inconclusive failures, and any baseline failure ⇒ treated as affected (fail closed) with the reason recorded.
- **Risk: a permissive "Yes" leaks into the release.** Mitigated by AC6 (ship passes `--strict`) and AC7 (strict never reuses a permissive verdict).
- **Risk: recursion/concurrency** — the baseline run must reuse `paced_runner()` and honour `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`; tests must mock subprocess execution (per the shared test-writing guidelines: no real suite, no real `audit_runner.py issue` child).
- **Assumption:** "integration/end-to-end" is identified by path convention in this repo (no markers exist); richer classification (markers, per-repo globs) is a follow-up if needed.
- **Assumption:** excused failures still create critical `test-failure` items (triage behaviour unchanged).
- **Assumption:** the merge gate proceeds with integration in permissive mode when the only failures are excused, recording them in the merge-gate evidence (strict keeps failing closed).
- **Assumption:** `--strict` is a generic audit-strictness flag; future strictness checks may join it, so the flag is not named after tests.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MSAAUJ1F0026BMN** – Create 'test' skill: run tests, triage failures, validate & fix test usefulness (completed) — the suite execution/triage machinery this change consumes (`run_tests.py`, `parse_pytest_failures`, `check_or_create`).

- **SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** – Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line (completed) — the freshness gate extended here with mode strength.
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** – Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits (open) — touches the same audit-runner verdict/lifecycle surface; check for conflicts when implementing.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** – Audit accepts gate-produced full-suite evidence (completed) — the read-only green-evidence path that permissive mode must not weaken.

### Repository file matches

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — audit contract documentation.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — suite execution, cache scope and triage semantics consumed by the audit.

- **Q1 (mode switch location):** strict default + `--permissive-tests` opt-in / **permissive default + `--strict` in ship** / env-var only. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **b** — permissive is the default and ship passes the strict flag; the flag is named **`--strict`** (not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness requirements can share it. # Intake brief — implement finish changed-scope gate always falls back to the full suite

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** chore (process/tooling; no gameplay behaviour change) ·
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (a), Q2 "as recommended" (= d), Q3 (a) on 2026-11-01.

**Decision (producer, 2026-11-01):** *verify-and-narrow*. The filed premise no
longer reproduces against the installed skills; this item now proves the scoped
gate works in a real `implement.py finish`, documents the node/vitest selection

**out of scope here** and filed on framework item **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**
(comment `SA-C0MVXW2CB8003BXPJ`); no agent-infrastructure edits from this repo.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` is documented to validate **changed scope only** for fast
iteration, but at filing time every finish gate in this repository logged
`changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and then ran
the full Vitest suite (≈ 346–409 s loaded, plus host-wide test-slot queueing).

Read-only verification during intake shows the **skill-level fix landed after
this item was filed** and the fallback no longer reproduces: the installed
selector maps vitest `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts` files and picks a subset for every one
of the last 25 commits. What has *not* happened is proof in a real gate (no
finish gate has run since the install), plus documentation and a measurement.
This item delivers exactly that proof.

## Users (user stories)

- *As an implementing agent*, I want `implement.py finish` on a single-file
  change to run only the affected tests, so the build → test → commit loop
  completes in minutes rather than queueing 1–2 h for a full-suite slot.
- *As a producer*, I want the changed-scope gate to still fail on a
  deliberately broken affected test, and the full suite to remain the
  `dev`-push gate, so speed never weakens correctness.
- *As a maintainer of this repo*, I want the node/vitest selection order
  documented so the behaviour is predictable and diagnosable.

## Existing state (verified 2026-11-01, read-only)

### The observed warning no longer exists in the installed skill

The filed log line —

```
WARNING: Implement run_tests: changed-scope selection unavailable in <worktree>
(no dev baseline, no changed tests, custom suiteCommands, or node-only selection)
```

— is the *old* generic message. All five matching logs under `.worklog/tmp/`
(2026-10-31 05:50 → 22:35) contain exactly that text. The installed message is

`changed-scope selection unavailable in <path> (<specific reason>)`.

- `implement.py` `_run_resolved_suite` → `_run_group_from_changed_files` →
  `_run_changed_scope_selection` (shared `run_tests.changed_scope_selection`)
  → full suite. The pytest-only `_run_changed_scope_pytest` path described in

- `run_tests.py` now (a) recognises `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` / `.js` / `.tsx`
  test files in `map_changed_to_tests`, (b) emits
  `node_modules/.bin/vitest run <files>` when the repo uses Vitest, and

  suite only). Docstrings cite **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**; the fix was committed
  2026-10-30 20:13 and installed here 2026-10-31 23:59 (`run_tests.py`) /
  2026-11-01 00:45 (`implement.py`) — **after** this item was filed (15:25 on
  2026-10-31) and after every observed fallback log.

- `run_tests.changed_scope_selection(<repo>)` over the changed file set of each

  (`selected 1 affected test file(s)` … `selected 18 affected test file(s)`).
- `changed_files={'src/core/GameState.ts'}` → `vitest run src/core/GameState.test.ts`;
